title: Mark Zuckerberg’s AI manifesto is exactly why people don’t like AI
slides: Zuckerberg's manifesto fuels AI backlash, but why?
He claims open-source AI is the only safe path.
Yet critics say it's just Meta's strategic play.
This shapes regulation, but not your daily tools.
Decide: judge AI by authors, not the tech itself.
thread_text:
1. The real AI power play

Meta's open-source push isn't about safety—it's a strategic move to shape regulation in their favor, while your daily tools stay unchanged.

2. Zuckerberg's safety claim

He says open-source AI is the only safe path, but critics see a bid to control the market, not protect users.

3. Regulation's hidden target

This debate is steering new AI laws, but those laws won't touch the AI you use every day—your search engine and autocomplete stay the same.

4. Who owns the narrative?

When tech giants preach safety, check their bottom line. The authors of AI policies often have the most to gain.

5. Your move: judge the source

Next time you read AI news, ask who benefits from the message. Does the author's stake change your view? Test it on this story.
